Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, has inaugurated the Kogi State All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, appointing himself chairman and former Senator Smart Adeyemi as Director-General ahead of the 2027 general elections. The inauguration was held on Tuesday at the Government House, Lokoja, according to a statement by the state Commissioner for Information, Kingsley Femi Fanwo. The statement said former Governor Yahaya Bello, former Governor Captain Idris Wada, former Deputy Governor Yomi Awoniyi and Chief Edward Onoja were named as campaign patrons. “Governor Ododo charged members of the council to place party unity above personal interests, describing collective responsibility, grassroots mobilisation and effective coordination as critical to the task ahead. “He said the APC must engage Nigerians with its record of achievements and vision for the future rather than political rhetoric, urging members to take the campaign message across the three senatorial districts, 21 local government areas, 239 wards and 3,508 polling units in Kogi State,” the statement said. Add us to your Preferred Sources The governor also highlighted President Bola Tinubu’s support for Kogi’s development, citing the approval of the Kogi International Airport, improved federal revenue allocations and other infrastructure initiatives as significant opportunities for the state. He listed ongoing projects and interventions in education, healthcare, roads, agriculture, security and youth empowerment as areas where his administration was translating available resources into tangible benefits for residents. “Ododo maintained that the relationship between the Federal Government and Kogi State had opened new development opportunities, stressing that another four years of collaboration could further expand infrastructure, investment, healthcare, education and economic opportunities,” the statement said. In his remarks, the Director-General, Adeyemi, commended the governor’s leadership and highlighted the Tinubu administration’s appointments of Kogi indigenes to important national positions, including ministerial and strategic institutional offices. Adeyemi also referenced the ongoing Kogi International Airport project, recalling how critics had previously questioned his appointment as Chairman of the Senate Committee on Aviation because the state had no airport. Other key appointments include Deputy Governor Joel Oyibo Salifu and Aliyu Ezzu Momoh as vice-chairmen; Ali Bello as council coordinator, with Hilary Ojomah Egwudah as deputy; and Kingsley Femi Fanwo as coordinating director, strategic communication. Majeed Dahiru was named state presidential campaign spokesman, while Abdulaziz Idris King, Suberu Adagu, Aliyu Umar Yusuf, Yakubu Yusuf Okala and Commander Jerry Omodara (retd.) were assigned responsibilities for election planning, administration, stakeholder mobilisation, logistics and security, respectively. “Governor Ododo congratulated the appointees and charged them to demonstrate commitment, discipline and integrity, stressing that the council’s success would be measured by effective grassroots engagement and a united party structure across the state,” the statement said.
